limitations: Historical FP32 CPU ORT rejection is preserved; both actual FP16 RKNN models also fail the original strict element gate. No threshold relaxation or output correction.

Same-process frame0 AB/BA/AB gives only two warm calls per method, with uncontrolled temperature/frequency; other two frames each run once per method. No percentile, sustained throughput or end-to-end gain claim.

Ordinary timed calls include packing, inputs_set, run, outputs_get, owned FP32 copies and release. Preprocessing, loading, Update, correlation, geometry, hashing, statistics, file I/O and pose publication are excluded.
Separate instrumented profiles establish operator placement; their timings are not ordinary latency. CPU I/O profile rows do not measure all SDK output-get/conversion/copy overhead.
Spatial fmap relative L2 improves for the three sampled inputs and imap is unchanged, but first-frame fmap maximum absolute error increases. Neither metric establishes trajectory accuracy.
Saved representatives are independently read and recomputed; repeated unsaved calls rely on recorded raw-array metadata. Nine saved NPZ are not every SDK invocation.
Historical v26 CPU transpose profiles were recorded in a different run. Their comparison is diagnostic, not a controlled causal timing decomposition.
Resolution changes and sparse context outputs remain proposed experiments, not exported, benchmarked or trajectory-validated in v32.
External pretrained weights, ONNX/RKNN, SDK dependencies and dataset arrays are not published; source and weight licenses remain separate.
